coverage.text: Use if the document type needs more background (for example, explaining what an EOB is, or why closing disclosures matter). Skip for straightforward document types.
Use this sentence verbatim, adapting bracketed parts:
- Use "a few" when covering 3+ extraction methods; "a couple of" when covering 2.

Use ` ```json ` (always `json`, never `json5`). Include the `/* Sensible uses JSON5 to support in-line comments*/` header as the first line of the **first two code blocks only** — omit it from all subsequent blocks. Comments (` /* */ `) explain the "why", not the "what." Show a complete runnable snippet — include a full `{ "fields": [...] }` wrapper. Reader should be able to paste and go.
- **Factual, present tense**: Describe what the feature does, not what was built. "You can now extract…" not "We built extraction for…"
**Ordering**: Lead with the most significant features. Group by theme if it helps readability.
- Use bullets only when listing multiple parallel sub-items
Use readme short-link format — not full URLs. The prefix depends on which directory the file lives in, and the slug is the filename minus `.md`:

Only include images if URLs are explicitly provided. No trailing `
` unless it immediately precedes an image.
Use bold "**Limitations:**" (not an H2) followed by a bullet list when there are hard constraints on the feature. Place this in the opening section, not as a footer.
Use `## Notes` (H2) for miscellaneous callouts that don't fit in the body. For very short notes lists, use bold `**Notes**` (not H2) followed by bullets.
Use fenced ` ```json ` blocks. Inline `/* */` comments are acceptable (never `//`) — Sensible accepts relaxed JSON.
Always use `![Click to enlarge]`. Images live in `assets/images/final/`.

Use this rubric to compare two versions of the same docs section, for example a new draft against the published page, or a skill's output against an earlier hand-written draft. Copy the template into the work's session folder (`.claude/sessions/<work>/rubric.md`), fill it in, and commit it to the docs PR.

2. **Answer each question with a probability.** Write a number between 0 and 1 that the answer is yes, to two decimal places. Don't add up the probabilities or average them: the questions overlap, so a total double counts.
Use this template when creating a new Sensible integration guide. Replace all `[PLACEHOLDER]` text. Comments in `<!-- -->` are guidance — remove them from the final file.
- Don't start with "In this guide" or "This guide will show you."
- Always use `![Click to enlarge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sensible-hq/sensible-docs/v0/assets/images/final/[filename].png)`.
- Omit the "Zap 1 / Zap 2" headings
- Use a single `## Configure [Platform]` section for the main steps

**Cross-references:** Link to related pages when mentioning a named concept: `[Match object](doc:match)`, `[types](doc:types)`, `[JsonLogic](doc:jsonlogic)`, `[context](doc:prompt)`.
Use this sparingly — only when multiple parameters have documented incompatibilities that would clutter individual description cells.
Use this pattern when a method's parameter table includes a global param for completeness but the full description lives on the method object page.
Capitalize parameter names as Title Case when referring to them by name in running text:

Always use fenced ` ```json ` blocks. Inline comments in JSON configs (using `/* */`, never `//`) are acceptable and encouraged for complex configs — they help readers understand non-obvious choices. The Sensible engine accepts relaxed JSON.
